page: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at up to 3.525 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system includes 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for stateful operations. In addition to networked Premium Storage capabilities, the instance bundles 322 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage. It operates without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute potential, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25% at 2,702.89 points. Multi-core operations align closely with the median for its tier, yielding a stress-ng score of 10,805.45 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,838.0. In memory tests, cached reads reach 515.05 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read (38.15 GB/sec) and write (22.67 GB/sec) bandwidth metrics drop into the lower quartile. In transactional caching evaluations, the instance sustains 8.2 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a PassMark database operations score of 3,544.21.

By delivering a high memory-to-core allocation alongside bundled fast local SSD scratch space, the E8ads_v5 achieves cost-effective resource utilization for applications bounded primarily by memory footprint rather than uncached memory bandwidth or raw GPU parallelization. This configuration makes the instance well suited for relational and in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-intensive CI/CD test runners, and intermediate ETL pipeline staging.
description: Microsoft Azure E8ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz across 8 dedicated vCPUs and 4 physical cores. It provides 64.0 GB of memory alongside an integrated 322 GB local SSD for high-speed temporary storage. Performance benchmarks indicate upper-quartile single-core CPU throughput alongside consistent median-tier multi-threaded processing, compiling, and Redis caching rates exceeding 8.2 million operations per second. However, large-block uncached memory bandwidth benchmarks place in the lower quartile, presenting a potential throughput bottleneck for unbounded streaming memory transfers. With its balanced 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation, this instance represents an efficient infrastructure option for in-memory databases, Redis caches, mid-tier relational database hosting, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
